transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-09-24
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: Yes
Notes: Deck shared (link: https://redwood.app/decks/verdigris-poc) ; benchmark sheet (link: https://sheets.redwood/bench-verdigris)

Auto-summary: Quick alignment on scope: traffic topology, token-length mosaic, concurrency quantiles, SLA gating. Agreed to run 2x 1-hour benchmark passes (steady + burst) against hosted endpoint then evaluate dedicated sizing if needed.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Mason, I'm the AE working with Verdigris, and with me is Priya Patel our SE. How are you folks doing?
[00:07] Carlos: Good, yes thanks. Carlos here, head of ML. We got a pretty packed agenda — want to make sure we can validate throughput and tail later, and also sanity-check any data residency constraints.
[00:15] Mei: Hi, Mei from platform. We'll want to know if the pilot will require VPC peering or if we can go via private endpoint; also curious on key management.
[00:22] Priya: Great, quick outline: we'll cover traffic shape, token distribution (input vs output), concurrency and QPS mapping, success criteria, then benchmark plan and timelines. Sound ok?
[00:30] Liam: Yep, sounds good.
[00:33] Jordan: Quick qualifier — what's your current production QPS for the payments NLP endpoint? Average and peaks?
[00:38] Carlos: Right now we have a low baseline — around 2-3 rps average per region, but spikes during batch settlement and fraud windows push us to about 120 rps for 2-3 minutes, and sporadic microbursts hitting 400 rps for a few seconds. It's ephemeral but it matters for tail latencies.
[00:57] Priya: Good to know. When you say tokens, what's the typical input length vs response length? Do you log tokens or just bytes?
[01:05] Carlos: We log bytes, not tokens. That's one reason we need help — our current infra uses a hosted provider and cost is creeping. Average payload is ~650 bytes input, responses vary but usually short, 20-60 tokens. However, there are flows — like chargeback explanations — that produce 300-800 tokens on the output.
[01:25] Jordan: Ok that suggests a bimodal token distribution. Priya, can you sketch how we'd translate bytes into token estimates for the benchmark generator?
[01:33] Priya: Sure — we'll use a tokenizer sample on 1k records to estimate tokens per byte per language/format. For English prose here it's roughly 4 bytes per token on average, but because you have structured JSON + metadata, effective ratio will vary. We'll include three tiers: short (<=64 tokens output), medium (64-256), and long (256-800). We'll also simulate prefix caching for the common 2-step auth prompts.
[01:55] Mei: About caching — can Redwood do prefix KV cache sharing across requests to save compute on repeated system prompt prefixes?
[02:03] Priya: Yes, we support prefix/KV cache and can keep warm cache per session. For the pilot we'll test with cache enabled and disabled to measure cost delta. There might be transcription glitches in our docs — sometimes 'KV cahce' shows up in exports haha.
[02:20] Carlos: Ha, I saw that too.
[02:23] Jordan: Back to success criteria — what are your gating metrics? Is it latency first, cost, or quality?
[02:29] Liam: Product wants sub-250ms P50 and sub-500ms P95 for the short-response flows. For the long outputs we accept higher P50~1s and P95 up to 3s, but P99 should be reasonably bounded. Costs target is a 20% reduction vs our current provider on equivalent quality, or same cost with 10% better latency.
[02:50] Carlos: Also accuracy/quality: we have a set of 200 golden prompts for semantic fidelity — if outputs degrade beyond our baseline BLEU-like metric by more than 3% we consider it a regression.
[03:05] Priya: Good to have definitive success criteria. We'll incorporate quality gating in the benchmark harness. For throughput modelling: we need to map your burst patterns into concurrency. If your average request latency under load is L, then concurrency = QPS * L (Little's law).
[03:20] Mei: So for example at 120 rps with 300ms average latency we'd need 36 concurrent tokens? I -- well concurrent requests?
[03:28] Priya: Right, 120 * 0.3 = 36 concurrent requests. But token-level concurrency matters too for memory footprint (KV cache and kv state). For long outputs the compute time per token increases sustained concurrency usage.
[03:42] Jordan: We'll propose two pilot buckets: steady-state (matching your 2-3 rps baseline) and burst simulation (sustained 120 rps for 5 minutes, plus microbursts up to 400 rps for 20s). We'll measure tail latencies and cost per 1M tokens.
[03:57] Carlos: For benchmarking dataset — we can anonymize and send ~72 hours of traffic. Would that be enough?
[04:03] Priya: Yes. Ideally include request timestamps, response size bytes, endpoint type, and whether session had KV cache warm. We'll need a schema — I'll post the expected CSV format.
[04:12] Jordan: Also, question on routing — if we start with hosted but find we need dedicated GPUs for stable tail, what is the path?
[04:18] Priya: We can run the benchmark on hosted first. If test shows sustained GPU saturation or unacceptable tail, Redwood Dedicated sizing will be estimated, and we can propose a dedicated pool. The orchestration supports canary and fallback to hosted if dedicated has issues.
[04:32] Mei: Data residency — can the pilot keep logs in our VPC? We need audit logs to stay inside region eu-west-1.
[04:38] Jordan: For Private deployments we can do VPC and on-prem options. For a hosted pilot we can arrange regional hosting with restricted log export. We'll follow up with security docs.
[04:46] Carlos: On encryption — KMS integration is mandatory for us. Do you support customer-managed keys?
[04:50] Priya: Yes, Redwood supports KMS/HSM integration in Private and Dedicated. For hosted we can integrate customer keys for some artifacts; we'll detail the limits in the security packet.
[04:59] Liam: Ok, timeline questions: We'd like a 6-week pilot; what's realistic?
[05:03] Jordan: Typical pilot is 4-8 weeks. Proposed plan: week 0: traffic ingestion + payload generator; week 1: baseline benchmark (hosted); week 2: steady-state + burst runs; week 3: analyze results and quality gating; week 4-5: iterate (if dedicated candidate, size and provision), week 6: final report and rollout recommendation.
[05:25] Carlos: Fine. What's required from us to start now?
[05:28] Priya: We need the sample traffic, decision on success criteria (you gave them), a security contact for SOC2/KMS artifacts, and a point who can approve short-term test keys. Also confirm region and expected SLA for the pilot.
[05:40] Mei: I'll be that person for platform and we can host test keys.
[05:43] Aisha: SRE will audit the load generator; want to make sure we don't trigger rate limits accidentally.
[05:49] Priya: We'll throttle local generators and run gradual ramp. We'll also provide a sandbox API key with token limits.
[05:56] Jordan: Competitors question — any reason you might prefer Anthropic or OpenAI? Is it familiarity, cost, or a specific feature?
[06:04] Carlos: Mainly familiarity and tooling integrations. Also pricing unpredictability with usage-based models has been painful. If Redwood shows predictable unit economics and a plan to keep quality we can pivot.
[06:15] Priya: Noted. We'll include cost-per-1M-token estimates for both hosted and dedicated and expected tail-latency tradeoffs.
[06:23] Jordan: Bench specifics: we'll run two passes — steady 1 hour at baseline QPS, then 1 hour burst pass with scripted microbursts. For each we'll capture P50/P95/P99, CPU/GPU util, and cold-start times. We'll also measure cost per 1M input + output tokens.
[06:40] Carlos: Do you simulate model variants/quantization? Our concern: quantized models may drop quality.
[06:46] Priya: We'll test two model profiles: full-precision and int8/quantized variant. Quality gating will compare outputs to your golden set. If quantization drops quality beyond your threshold we won't recommend it.
[06:58] Mei: For concurrency mapping, can you produce a sizing table: qps -> required concurrency -> recommended GPU pool size?
[07:05] Priya: Yes, that's part of the deliverable. We'll produce a 'traffic topology matrix' that maps QPS buckets and token-length distributions to GPU footprints and expected cost band.
[07:16] Jordan: I want to note a transcribe oddity — sometimes our exports show 'Reedwood' instead of Redwood; ignore that.
[07:22] Carlos: Noted.
[07:23] Priya: Any other constraints? On-call windows, maintenance blackout windows?
[07:27] Aisha: We have nightly batch windows from 02:00-03:00 UTC where production is sensitive; avoid heavy stress tests in that window.
[07:35] Jordan: Ok. We'll avoid your blackout window and schedule benchmark runs during agreed periods.
[07:40] Liam: On the report format — include graphs for token length CDF, inter-arrival distribution, burst duty cycles, and tail maps.
[07:48] Priya: Yes, the benchmark report will include CDFs for input/output tokens, interarrival histograms, concurrency heatmap and cost breakdown by component (compute, memory, cache). We'll also attach a spreadsheet with per-run logs.
[07:59] Carlos: Are there any SI/ops costs for Dedicated provisioning we should budget for?
[08:04] Jordan: We'll include one-time setup and estimated monthly reserved pool costs in the SOW. Example numbers will be preliminary until we size after the benchmark.
[08:12] Mei: For the sample traffic, we'll anonymize PII. Do you need explicit mapping of original IDs?
[08:18] Priya: No, just keep schema consistent. We'll need session IDs to simulate KV cache reuse. If sessions are stripped we'll default to random session reuse which changes cache behavior, so try to keep session affinity.
[08:32] Carlos: Good call. We'll include session_id, timestamp, request_bytes, response_bytes, route, and "cache_hit" boolean if available.
[08:41] Jordan: Ok that's the data schema. Priya will upload an example CSV template after the call.
[08:46] Priya: I'll also upload the payload generator repo link and instructions: https://github.com/redwood-inference/payload-gen (note: link may be internal).
[08:54] Liam: Any constraints on model choice? We primarily use an instruction-tuned LLM for classification and summarization.
[08:59] Priya: We'll propose model families that match your quality bar; we'll run quality comparisons across 2-3 candidate variants. For cost we might test a trimmed variant.
[09:08] Carlos: For long outputs we worry about token streaming latency; do you stream tokens?
[09:12] Priya: Yes, Redwood supports streaming and chunked responses. For long outputs we'll compare total wall-clock latency with and without streaming to account for time-to-first-token vs time-to-complete.
[09:24] Aisha: Rate limiting concerns — can the sandbox reflect production rate limits?
[09:28] Jordan: We'll mirror production limits but allow elevated limits for controlled benchmark windows.
[09:32] Mei: About observability — can we get token-level tracing per request? Memory footprint per session?
[09:37] Priya: We'll provide detailed traces in the console for benchmark runs, including per-request token counts, kernel utilization, mem usage, and tail latency traces. We'll redact any sensitive text.
[09:47] Carlos: Great. If we hit unacceptable tail behaviors, is there an automated fallback to a smaller model or region?
[09:53] Priya: Redwood supports routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants; we can configure a canary that falls back to a lower-cost or more stable model under stress. We'll test that as part of the run.
[10:05] Jordan: Let's capture explicit success criteria to put in the SOW: 1) short-flow P95 <500ms; 2) long-flow P95 <3s; 3) cost <= 0.8x current provider for equivalent quality or quality within 3% of baseline BLEU metric; 4) no security blockers on KMS/SOC2. Agree?
[10:20] Carlos: Agree. 3% threshold is strict but ok.
[10:24] Jordan: Any blockers to start?
[10:26] Mei: We'll prepare anonymized traffic and confirm region. No blocker.
[10:29] Aisha: I need the security packet before any keys are provisioned.
[10:33] Jordan: We'll share security docs and SOC2 artifacts; security packet will be published to the shared drive.
[10:40] Priya: I'll draft the benchmark sheet now, will include run scripts and expected metrics.
[10:44] Liam: Can we schedule the benchmark for Oct 6th at 09:00 UTC?
[10:48] Jordan: Tentative — Jordan will confirm after SOW.
[10:50] Carlos: Fine.
[10:51] Jordan: Ok let's recap next steps — (1) Priya share payload generator + CSV template, (2) Verdigris to share sample traffic, (3) Jordan to share SOW and pricing, (4) schedule benchmark run for first week of October. Any other?
[11:05] Carlos: That's it from us.
[11:07] Jordan: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email and link the sheet.
[11:12] End of recording
